subject: design-technology
title: Technical Textiles in Medicine and Sport
welcome_lead: From compression bandages to F1 driver suits.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: technical textiles in medical and sporting applications.

concepts.def: Textile engineered for healthcare (bandages, sutures, scaffolds).
Tight-fitting garment applying pressure (medical or sport).
Textile with integrated electronic or responsive function.
Material whose Poisson's ratio is negative — widens when stretched.
Material absorbing/releasing latent heat at a fixed temperature.
Material safely absorbed by the body over time.

walkthroughs.body_html: Modern medical textiles include silicone-elastomer dressings, antimicrobial sutures, vascular grafts (Dacron, PTFE) and bioresorbable meshes that scaffold tissue regrowth then dissolve.
Compression sportswear (Skins, 2CKU) claims to reduce muscle vibration. F1 driver suits meet FIA 8856-2018 — flame resistance to over 800 °C for 11 seconds, using multi-layer Nomex.
PCM-filled fibres (Outlast, from NASA research) store body heat and release it later. Auxetic textiles widen when stretched — used in protective sportswear (D3O, Auxetix).
